description: HTTP-level conformance cases for the control-plane read tier (#617). Any control plane serving the canonical conformance fixture project must reproduce these normalized responses. Run: python ../runner.py --base-url <url>.

python-cp.description: The Python control plane (packages/python, serve-python.sh) — the baseline recorder; the shared goldens are its responses.

ts-cp.description: The TypeScript control plane (packages/typescript/temporal-controlplane, serve-typescript.sh). Cases with an editions.ts-cp variant diverge BY DESIGN (mirror registry identity, capability honesty until the operate tier, dialect artifacts); skips point at live projection-gap issues.

normalize.note: Values of these fields are machine/run-specific (absolute paths, timestamps) and compare as <normalized>; per-case 'mask' JSON Pointers (with * wildcards) handle structural cases like bundle git provenance (/code) and absolute file paths inside arrays. The bundle case additionally masks the workflow-binding-opaque identity fields (/workflow/workflow_type, /workflow/spec_digest, /workflow/spec_digest_algorithm, /workflow/generator_version): these differ BY DESIGN across runtime bindings (per contracts/temporal-binding) — the Python and TypeScript control planes derive them from their own binding, so they are not cross-runtime comparable. Schema-identity decision (#644): a slot's `name` is the LOGICAL type name both editions agree on (the contract requires it; the TS `schemas:` ref prefix was a loader artifact, fixed); `hash`/`json_schema` shape and the Python-only `module` key (an untyped-dict recording detail, not contract surface) are edition-native by design — the same class as the binding digests.

open.description: Default open authorizer: every caller holds all permissions.

proxy.description: Proxy-header authorizer (trust-proxy-auth): actor + permissions from X-Typeflux-Actor / X-Typeflux-Permissions.

token.description: Bearer-token authorizer with the canonical conformance grants (NAME:PERMS:TOKEN syntax).
